Marketing teams are asked to prove campaign ROI, but the numbers usually live in five separate logins. We design custom marketing dashboards that put campaign performance, traffic, and spend on one screen, built in Power BI or Tableau around the metrics your team actually reports on.

[/vc_column_text][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][dfd_delimiter delimiter_style="dfd-delimiter-with-icon" icon_size="30" delimiter_border_style="dotted" icon_fontawesome="fa fa-solid fa-circle-arrow-down" show_icon="enable_icon" delim_line_color="#4a48601C" icon_color="#c39f76" icon_hover_color="#e9e9e9"][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="35" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="35" screen_tablet_spacer_size="35" screen_mobile_spacer_size="35"][vc_single_image image="39240" img_size="large" alignment="center" css=""][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="60" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="60" screen_tablet_spacer_size="60" screen_mobile_spacer_size="60"][dfd_heading enable_delimiter="" style="style_02" heading_margin="margin-bottom:20px;" subtitle="The straight answer" title_font_options="tag:h2|font_size:70|line_height:64" subtitle_font_options="tag:h3|font_size:38|line_height:32"]

What is a marketing dashboard?

[/dfd_heading][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][vc_column_text css=""]

Campaign, traffic, and spend data usually live in separate logins — a marketing dashboard puts them on one screen your team actually opens every week. We design these for you, built around your existing data sources in Power BI or Tableau instead of a generic template.

The Datalabs Agency is a Melbourne-based data visualization consultancy founded in 2012 that delivers corporate training workshops (Power BI, Tableau, data storytelling), dashboard design, and BI style guides for clients including Mercedes-Benz, Adidas, and UPS.

[/vc_column_text][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="80" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="80" screen_tablet_spacer_size="80" screen_mobile_spacer_size="80"][dfd_heading enable_delimiter="" style="style_02" heading_margin="margin-bottom:20px;" subtitle="Custom vs off-the-shelf" title_font_options="tag:h2|font_size:70|line_height:64" subtitle_font_options="tag:h3|font_size:38|line_height:32"]

How is a custom dashboard different from a template?

[/dfd_heading][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][vc_column_text css=""]

A template ships with someone else’s chart choices and default metrics. A custom marketing dashboard starts from your campaigns, channels, and reporting cadence, so every chart on the page answers the question your team actually asks each week.

Templates are a reasonable starting point for a small team moving off spreadsheets — our Power BI templates exist for exactly that. A template cannot know that your team tracks cost per lead by channel, or that leadership only cares about three numbers out of a twelve-tab report. A custom-built dashboard is scoped around your actual KPIs and your actual data sources, built to the metrics your team already reports on. That difference matters most once a team outgrows the basics: more campaigns, more channels, and a report that used to take an afternoon to assemble by hand.

[/vc_column_text][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="60" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="60" screen_tablet_spacer_size="60" screen_mobile_spacer_size="60"][dfd_button button_text="Get a dashboard quote" buttom_link_src="url:https%3A%2F%2Fwww.datalabsagency.com%2Fcontact-us%2F|||" style="style_6" background="#8a8f6a" hover_background="#4e5041" border="border-style:none;|border-radius:5px;" hover_border="border-style:none;|border-radius:5px;"][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner el_class="dfd_col-tablet-12" width="1/4" offset="vc_col-lg-3 vc_col-md-2 vc_col-xs-1"][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="40" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="40" screen_tablet_spacer_size="40" screen_mobile_spacer_size="40"][/vc_column][/vc_row] [vc_row bg_check="row-background-dark" dfd_enable_overlay="" dfd_row_config="full_width_content_paddings" el_id="pat-section-1"][vc_column][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="40" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="40" screen_tablet_spacer_size="40" screen_mobile_spacer_size="40"][vc_row_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/4"][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/2"][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="40" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="40" screen_tablet_spacer_size="40" screen_mobile_spacer_size="40"][dfd_heading enable_delimiter="" style="style_02" heading_margin="margin-bottom:20px;" subtitle="Built around your channels" title_font_options="tag:h2|font_size:70|line_height:64" subtitle_font_options="tag:h3|font_size:38|line_height:32"]

What goes into a marketing dashboard?

[/dfd_heading][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][vc_column_text css=""]

Campaign performance, website traffic, spend against budget, and channel comparison usually sit side by side on a marketing dashboard. We choose the chart types and layout around the decisions your team makes each week, instead of a fixed set of default widgets.

This follows the same process behind our wider dashboard design service: sketch the layout before styling it, then build in whichever tool your data already lives in.

[/vc_column_text][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/4"][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][/vc_column][vc_column][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][/vc_column][/vc_row] [vc_row bg_check="row-background-dark" dfd_enable_overlay="" dfd_row_config="full_width_content_paddings" el_id="pat-section-2"][vc_column][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="40" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="40" screen_tablet_spacer_size="40" screen_mobile_spacer_size="40"][vc_row_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/4"][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/2"][dfd_heading enable_delimiter="" style="style_02" heading_margin="margin-bottom:20px;" subtitle="Marketing has its own KPIs" title_font_options="tag:h2|font_size:70|line_height:64" subtitle_font_options="tag:h3|font_size:38|line_height:32"]

How is this different from a general BI dashboard?

[/dfd_heading][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][vc_column_text css=""]

Marketing gets its own dashboard because its metrics change weekly: campaign, traffic, and spend numbers your team actually reports on. A general BI dashboard usually mixes finance, operations, and sales metrics that only a few people ever open.

Scoping a dashboard to one function is a design decision. A dashboard trying to serve marketing, finance, and operations at once tends to serve none of them well — too many metrics compete for the same screen, and nobody can find the one number they actually track that week. Building a marketing-specific view means every chart on the page answers a question a marketer actually asks.

[/vc_column_text][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/4"][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][/vc_column][vc_column][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="40" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="40" screen_tablet_spacer_size="40" screen_mobile_spacer_size="40"][/vc_column][/vc_row] [vc_row bg_check="row-background-dark" dfd_enable_overlay="" dfd_row_config="full_width_content_paddings" el_id="pat-table"][vc_column][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="40" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="40" screen_tablet_spacer_size="40" screen_mobile_spacer_size="40"][vc_row_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/6"][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="2/3"][dfd_heading enable_delimiter="" style="style_02" heading_margin="margin-bottom:20px;" subtitle="Compare your options" title_font_options="tag:h2|font_size:70|line_height:64" subtitle_font_options="tag:h3|font_size:38|line_height:32"]

Template, workshop, or custom dashboard — which fits?

[/dfd_heading][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][vc_column_text css=""]

The right option depends on whether you want a dashboard delivered, or the skills to build one yourselves.

[/vc_column_text][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/6"][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][/vc_column][vc_column][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="40" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="40" screen_tablet_spacer_size="40" screen_mobile_spacer_size="40"][/vc_column][/vc_row] [vc_row bg_check="row-background-dark" dfd_enable_overlay="" el_id="pat-faq"][vc_column width="1/4"][/vc_column][vc_column width="1/2"][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="40" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="40" screen_tablet_spacer_size="40" screen_mobile_spacer_size="40"][vc_column_text css="" item_animation="transition.fadeIn"]

Questions & Answers

Marketing dashboards

[/vc_column_text][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="40" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="30" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][dfd_accordion style="style-3" active_section="1" font_size="18" tab_title_google_fonts="yes" tab_title_custom_fonts="font_family:Arvo%3Aregular%2Citalic%2C700%2C700italic|font_style:700%20bold%20regular%3A700%3Anormal" icon_size="14"][vc_tta_section title="What is a marketing dashboard?" tab_id="1685677784578-172f9372-59216fce-87a69a68-2eae"][vc_column_text css=""]

Think of a marketing dashboard as one screen for the campaign performance, website traffic, and spend data that usually sits in separate platforms and logins. Instead of rebuilding a report every month, your team opens a dashboard that already reflects your Power BI or Tableau data, however you already track it.

[/vc_column_text][/vc_tta_section][vc_tta_section title="What platforms do you build marketing dashboards in?" tab_id="1685677784323-438be9dd-da0e6fce-87a69a68-2eae"][vc_column_text css=""]

Your dashboard goes wherever your data already lives, most commonly Power BI or Tableau. The goal is a dashboard your team keeps using, built around your existing reporting tools.

[/vc_column_text][/vc_tta_section][vc_tta_section title="How much does a custom marketing dashboard cost?" tab_id="1685677784395-526dd6ff-b9c26fce-87a69a68-2eae"][vc_column_text css=""]

There is no single marketing-dashboard rate card — every build is scoped to your data sources and KPIs and quoted as a fixed project cost once we understand the brief. The closest published reference points are our AU$250 per hour data visualisation consulting rate and the AU$3,000 to $8,000 per workshop day range for a facilitated build session; ask for a quote for your specific dashboard.

[/vc_column_text][/vc_tta_section][vc_tta_section title="Do you offer a workshop instead of a custom build?" tab_id="1685677784507-83427dcb-7a756fce-87a69a68-2eae"][vc_column_text css=""]

Yes. If you want the skill in-house, our Designing Great Dashboards workshop teaches the same design principles as a live team session, starting at AU$4,600 for a remote half-day.

[/vc_column_text][/vc_tta_section][vc_tta_section title="Can you build the dashboard around our existing campaign data?" tab_id="1786584255290-781b75e9-21a0"][vc_column_text css=""]

Yes. We connect the dashboard to your existing data sources and reporting tools instead of asking you to change how your team already tracks campaigns. That is the difference between a template and a dashboard built for your channels specifically.

[/vc_column_text][/vc_tta_section][vc_tta_section title="Can you build an AI-powered marketing dashboard?" tab_id="faq-mdash-ai-2026"][vc_column_text css=""]

Two different things are meant by that, and both are on offer. AI-assisted design means the dashboard is designed and built with AI in the loop, which is how a custom build now moves faster than it used to. AI inside the dashboard means it can be built so your team asks questions in plain language instead of only reading the charts. Either way the result is a Power BI or Tableau dashboard your team owns.

[/vc_column_text][/vc_tta_section][/dfd_accordion][vc_raw_html][/vc_raw_html][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="40" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="30" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][dfd_button button_text="Get a dashboard quote" buttom_link_src="url:https%3A%2F%2Fwww.datalabsagency.com%2Fcontact-us%2F|||" style="style_6" background="#8a8f6a" hover_background="#4e5041" border="border-style:none;|border-radius:5px;" hover_border="border-style:none;|border-radius:5px;"][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="40" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="30" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][/vc_column][vc_column width="1/4"][/vc_column][/vc_row] [vc_row bg_check="row-background-dark" css=".vc_custom_1691550358421{background-color: #2f2e3a !important;}" el_id="pat-article-1"][vc_column width="1/6"][/vc_column][vc_column width="4/6"][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="60" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="40" screen_tablet_spacer_size="30" screen_mobile_spacer_size="40"][dfd_heading enable_delimiter="" style="style_02" heading_margin="margin-bottom:20px;" subtitle="Start with the questions, not the charts" title_font_options="tag:h2|font_size:70|line_height:64" subtitle_font_options="tag:h3|font_size:38|line_height:32"]

How we design a marketing dashboard

[/dfd_heading][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="15" screen_mobile_spacer_size="19"][vc_row_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/2"][vc_column_text css=""]

I start every marketing dashboard project with a short conversation, not a data pull. What does your team actually decide with this data each week? Which campaigns get paused, which channels get more budget, which numbers go in the Monday report? Those answers decide the layout long before I open Power BI or Tableau.

Most marketing teams already track plenty of numbers — impressions, clicks, spend, conversions, cost per lead — spread across five or six platforms. The dashboard’s job is not to show every metric available. It puts the handful your team actually acts on in one place, arranged so the story is obvious at a glance instead of buried in a table. The metrics that do not survive that cut are usually the ones nobody has opened since the platform first started reporting them, and are never the ones a team misses.

[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/2"][vc_column_text css=""]

I sketch the layout before touching colour or chart type. A campaign-comparison view, a spend-versus-budget tracker and a channel breakdown need three different chart shapes, not one template stretched across all three. Getting the layout right first is what stops the finished dashboard becoming another report nobody opens.

Once the layout is agreed, the build happens in whichever tool your data already lives in. If your team reports out of Power BI, that is where the dashboard lives — see our Power BI dashboard design work. Tableau builds follow the same process.

Dashboards still in use long after a project ends answer a real question every time someone opens them. The target: a tool your team opens on a Monday morning, never a showcase piece.

Who's behind these dashboard designs

[/dfd_heading][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="15" screen_mobile_spacer_size="19"][vc_column_text css=""]

I founded The Datalabs Agency in 2012, in Melbourne, after learning visual storytelling at National Geographic. That background shapes how I still think about a marketing dashboard: it is a piece of visual communication first, and a data connection second.

Since then I have built dashboards and BI style guides for clients including Mercedes-Benz, Adidas, and UPS, alongside corporate training workshops in Power BI, Tableau — see our Tableau dashboard design work — and data storytelling. Marketing dashboards are one of the more common requests: every marketing team eventually needs proof of what a campaign actually did.

I still get involved directly in design decisions on every project. Dashboard work, especially the marketing kind, rewards someone who has sat through enough campaign reviews to know which number actually changes a decision and which one just fills a slide.

What’s next in data visualization? I think you know where this is going: artificial intelligence. Where am I going with the Datalabs Agency? Same answer.

Marketing teams are asked to prove campaign ROI, but the numbers usually live in five separate logins. We design custom marketing dashboards that put campaign performance, traffic, and spend on one screen, built in Power BI or Tableau around the metrics your team actually reports on.

The straight answer

What is a marketing dashboard?

[vc_column_text css=””]

Campaign, traffic, and spend data usually live in separate logins — a marketing dashboard puts them on one screen your team actually opens every week. We design these for you, built around your existing data sources in Power BI or Tableau instead of a generic template.

The Datalabs Agency is a Melbourne-based data visualization consultancy founded in 2012 that delivers corporate training workshops (Power BI, Tableau, data storytelling), dashboard design, and BI style guides for clients including Mercedes-Benz, Adidas, and UPS.

[/vc_column_text]

Custom vs off-the-shelf

How is a custom dashboard different from a template?

[vc_column_text css=””]

A template ships with someone else’s chart choices and default metrics. A custom marketing dashboard starts from your campaigns, channels, and reporting cadence, so every chart on the page answers the question your team actually asks each week.

Templates are a reasonable starting point for a small team moving off spreadsheets — our Power BI templates exist for exactly that. A template cannot know that your team tracks cost per lead by channel, or that leadership only cares about three numbers out of a twelve-tab report. A custom-built dashboard is scoped around your actual KPIs and your actual data sources, built to the metrics your team already reports on. That difference matters most once a team outgrows the basics: more campaigns, more channels, and a report that used to take an afternoon to assemble by hand.

[/vc_column_text]

Built around your channels

What goes into a marketing dashboard?

[vc_column_text css=””]

Campaign performance, website traffic, spend against budget, and channel comparison usually sit side by side on a marketing dashboard. We choose the chart types and layout around the decisions your team makes each week, instead of a fixed set of default widgets.

This follows the same process behind our wider dashboard design service: sketch the layout before styling it, then build in whichever tool your data already lives in.

[/vc_column_text]

Marketing has its own KPIs

How is this different from a general BI dashboard?

[vc_column_text css=””]

Marketing gets its own dashboard because its metrics change weekly: campaign, traffic, and spend numbers your team actually reports on. A general BI dashboard usually mixes finance, operations, and sales metrics that only a few people ever open.

Scoping a dashboard to one function is a design decision. A dashboard trying to serve marketing, finance, and operations at once tends to serve none of them well — too many metrics compete for the same screen, and nobody can find the one number they actually track that week. Building a marketing-specific view means every chart on the page answers a question a marketer actually asks.

[/vc_column_text]

Questions & Answers

Marketing dashboards

[/vc_column_text]
[dfd_accordion style=”style-3″ active_section=”1″ font_size=”18″ tab_title_google_fonts=”yes” tab_title_custom_fonts=”font_family:Arvo%3Aregular%2Citalic%2C700%2C700italic|font_style:700%20bold%20regular%3A700%3Anormal” icon_size=”14″][vc_tta_section title=”What is a marketing dashboard?” tab_id=”1685677784578-172f9372-59216fce-87a69a68-2eae”][vc_column_text css=””]

Think of a marketing dashboard as one screen for the campaign performance, website traffic, and spend data that usually sits in separate platforms and logins. Instead of rebuilding a report every month, your team opens a dashboard that already reflects your Power BI or Tableau data, however you already track it.

[/vc_column_text][/vc_tta_section][vc_tta_section title=”What platforms do you build marketing dashboards in?” tab_id=”1685677784323-438be9dd-da0e6fce-87a69a68-2eae”][vc_column_text css=””]

Your dashboard goes wherever your data already lives, most commonly Power BI or Tableau. The goal is a dashboard your team keeps using, built around your existing reporting tools.

[/vc_column_text][/vc_tta_section][vc_tta_section title=”How much does a custom marketing dashboard cost?” tab_id=”1685677784395-526dd6ff-b9c26fce-87a69a68-2eae”][vc_column_text css=””]

There is no single marketing-dashboard rate card — every build is scoped to your data sources and KPIs and quoted as a fixed project cost once we understand the brief. The closest published reference points are our AU$250 per hour data visualisation consulting rate and the AU$3,000 to $8,000 per workshop day range for a facilitated build session; ask for a quote for your specific dashboard.

[/vc_column_text][/vc_tta_section][vc_tta_section title=”Do you offer a workshop instead of a custom build?” tab_id=”1685677784507-83427dcb-7a756fce-87a69a68-2eae”][vc_column_text css=””]

Yes. If you want the skill in-house, our Designing Great Dashboards workshop teaches the same design principles as a live team session, starting at AU$4,600 for a remote half-day.

[/vc_column_text][/vc_tta_section][vc_tta_section title=”Can you build the dashboard around our existing campaign data?” tab_id=”1786584255290-781b75e9-21a0″][vc_column_text css=””]

Yes. We connect the dashboard to your existing data sources and reporting tools instead of asking you to change how your team already tracks campaigns. That is the difference between a template and a dashboard built for your channels specifically.

[/vc_column_text][/vc_tta_section][vc_tta_section title=”Can you build an AI-powered marketing dashboard?” tab_id=”faq-mdash-ai-2026″][vc_column_text css=””]

Two different things are meant by that, and both are on offer. AI-assisted design means the dashboard is designed and built with AI in the loop, which is how a custom build now moves faster than it used to. AI inside the dashboard means it can be built so your team asks questions in plain language instead of only reading the charts. Either way the result is a Power BI or Tableau dashboard your team owns.

[/vc_column_text][/vc_tta_section][/dfd_accordion][vc_raw_html][/vc_raw_html]

Start with the questions, not the charts

How we design a marketing dashboard

[vc_row_inner][vc_column_inner width=”1/2″][vc_column_text css=””]

I start every marketing dashboard project with a short conversation, not a data pull. What does your team actually decide with this data each week? Which campaigns get paused, which channels get more budget, which numbers go in the Monday report? Those answers decide the layout long before I open Power BI or Tableau.

Most marketing teams already track plenty of numbers — impressions, clicks, spend, conversions, cost per lead — spread across five or six platforms. The dashboard’s job is not to show every metric available. It puts the handful your team actually acts on in one place, arranged so the story is obvious at a glance instead of buried in a table. The metrics that do not survive that cut are usually the ones nobody has opened since the platform first started reporting them, and are never the ones a team misses.

[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width=”1/2″][vc_column_text css=””]

I sketch the layout before touching colour or chart type. A campaign-comparison view, a spend-versus-budget tracker and a channel breakdown need three different chart shapes, not one template stretched across all three. Getting the layout right first is what stops the finished dashboard becoming another report nobody opens.

Once the layout is agreed, the build happens in whichever tool your data already lives in. If your team reports out of Power BI, that is where the dashboard lives — see our Power BI dashboard design work. Tableau builds follow the same process.

Dashboards still in use long after a project ends answer a real question every time someone opens them. The target: a tool your team opens on a Monday morning, never a showcase piece.

[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner]

Founded in 2012, still hands-on

Who’s behind these dashboard designs

[vc_column_text css=””]

I founded The Datalabs Agency in 2012, in Melbourne, after learning visual storytelling at National Geographic. That background shapes how I still think about a marketing dashboard: it is a piece of visual communication first, and a data connection second.

Since then I have built dashboards and BI style guides for clients including Mercedes-Benz, Adidas, and UPS, alongside corporate training workshops in Power BI, Tableau — see our Tableau dashboard design work — and data storytelling. Marketing dashboards are one of the more common requests: every marketing team eventually needs proof of what a campaign actually did.

I still get involved directly in design decisions on every project. Dashboard work, especially the marketing kind, rewards someone who has sat through enough campaign reviews to know which number actually changes a decision and which one just fills a slide.

What’s next in data visualization? I think you know where this is going: artificial intelligence. Where am I going with the Datalabs Agency? Same answer.
